Bos Logistics - international removers or scam artists

By: Annalise Lubbe | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Moving abroad became a nightmare for a number of people from the Cape who trusted their precious cargo with international removers Bos Logistics, and paid the price.

Unique Selling Point:
How did one international removal company scam at least a dozen people we know of from Cape Town who planned to move abroad, into believing they are up to the job? Relocating to Canada, UAE, Germany, and England, the incompetence and skulduggery of Shane and Ciara O’Boyle left a trail of infuriated and disgruntled customers behind.


Summary:
An international move can be stressful and leave many people anxious. Selecting a reliable mover, who has your best interest at heart, is therefore vital. Sadly, many people fall victim to attractive pay-off lines such as: “Small enough to care, large enough to do it”, and “let our family move yours” - comforting words from Bos Logistics to lure them in.

Bos Logistics, an international relocation and freight forwarding Cape Town company was registered under the ownership of Shane Brown O’Boyle in February 2020. In 2019 26-year-old O’Boyle opened his doors for business together with his sister, Ciara.

We track the stories of several Cape Tonian families who were charmed by the young and confident Shane. Soon after payment they came to realise it was all false promises of insurance cover and expected shipping and delivery dates. It was endless guessing of where exactly their furniture was at any given time: did it in fact leave Cape Town? At which port was it held? Why was it not released? And why did some of their consignments get mixed up and ended up on another continent at someone else’s address?


Further information:
Case study one: Megan Ellis-Smith
In 2020 Megan Ellis-Smith and her husband Mike decided to emigrate to the UK. The elderly couple were anxious about the move: “It is not easy leaving your home, your country, your friends. And going across to another country and starting again”, said Megan. Their son Paul, found Bos Logistics on the internet. “They sounded professional and friendly, so we were very happy.” The quote from Shane came to R137 000 for door to door service which Megan accepted.

The couple left in May and were promised their furniture by July. In July a shortage of truck drivers in the Uk got the blame for non-delivery. In August they were told their furniture had arrived and were cleared by customs - no charge - which Megan thought suspicious as there is normally a fee involved. The next correspondence from Ciara was to inform them their goods were on a vessel but were not offloaded as it had skipped the port and there would be a six week delay. “So we waited some more. By this time Bos was starting to go underground and they wouldn’t answer emails, all their phone lines”, Megan said. With no communication Megan was at her wits end and asked a friend in Cape Town to visit their office in Claremont. All they found was an unmanned desk.

Megan became very suspicious and found a contact in the shipping industry to enquire if there was in fact a vessel with their goods on board. She waited for feedback.

By December Megan received a mail from Ciara to say the furniture was now on a ship called Santa Teresa, only to be told two days before the expected arrival date, that the booking was canceled. Megan and Mike then heard from their source that their goods never left Cape Town and were in fact still in fact sitting in Shane’s warehouse.

“So then we sent an email to Shane to say will you release our things, otherwise we will expose you to the Cape Time, the Argus….Carte Blanche, Hellopeter, Wendy Knola, Cirello the whole tutie, and then they responded quickly. So they say we have a container going we can load your goods or we can release your goods so we say release!” said Megan.

With the help of a new transport company from Cape Town the couple’s furniture were moved from Bos’s warehouse and shipped. It cost a mere R19 000 versus Bos’s R137 000 and it only took 5 weeks to arrive at their new home in the UK.

“I feel very strongly that Bos has lied to us all the way, avoided us and pretty much scammed us.”

Besides dealing with the traumatic experice of the removal company, they son Paul passed away the year they emigrated.

Case study two: Christelle and Wesley Elson
Christelle and Wesley Elson, a couple from Tableview in the Cape moved to Dresden Germany in September 2019. They contracted Bos Logistics to move their belongings - a company detail on Sierlo, an online platform providing online quotes and costs at the touch of a button. The site also provides reviews of companies but at the time there were hardly any as they were probably some of his earliest customers. (the company was only registered in 2020 but business started in 2019 as per the evidence of the Elson’s who contracted their services.)

They were quoted R30 725 for a full door to door service. The quote came with Marine All Risk Cover from OUTsurance policy to the value of R150 000. This gave the couple piece of mind.

In September Bos arrived at the Elson’s door to pack. Christelle remembered that first meetingg with Shane. “On the day they came to collect Shane was there to supervise and told us the packing list will be sent to us via email soon, that should have raised a red flag”. To this date they have not received the list.

December, no delivery was made. January, a wage strike was blamed. In February an email from Shane made the Elson’s very nervous. “We were informed that our goods would not be released due to a financial hold placed on Bos Logistics account with FNB (reason for this was suspected fraud). As a result the MSC Pegasus sent our goods back to South Africa”, quoted from Shane’s email. Was this a delay tactic? Where were their goods now? Did it actually leave Cape Town?

It took 9 months for their belongings to arrive. The couple were distressed. “Some items were missing which are totally irreplaceable”, said Christelle. Engagement and wedding photos; a nursery table handcrafted by a devoted father for his daughter made from American Ash were amongst the missing items.

“We immediately informed Shane that we would like to proceed with a claim to the insurance” said Wesley. To their shock, OUTsurance had no such policy on record.

In an email OUTsurance confirmed “the document is not authentic” and “we do not have marine insurance”. They will be reporting Bos Logistics to the Crime Insurance Bureau for producing a fraudulent document under their name.

Case study three: Split frame: Jan van der Westhuizen and Jade Rainbow from Dubai, and Sebastian Dockter from Canada
Sharing a container saves cost, which is why Jan van der Westhuizen, Jade Rainbow, and a third person from the Cape emigrating, shared a container. Destination? United Arab Emirates. In October the container were offloaded at the Jebel Ali Port in Dubai and their goods were stored in a warehouse nearby.

In the warehouse Jade was shocked at the condition in which she found her boxes. Items were peeling out and badly damaged. On closer inspection she even found a stranger’s goods inside. Toys belonging to her daughter were lying loose and some boxes were missing.

Jan found many of his boxes missing! It took much searching and eventually he used the internet as a tool. He found a Facebook page “Lost and found, Bos Logistics South Africa” started by Sebastian Dockter, another South African who relocated to Canada. He identified several of his items on the site and contacted Sebatian who told him ten of Jan’s boxes were delivered to his house marked Sebastian! Fortunately for Sebastian, one of his boxes was amongst Jan’s goods. At the same time Jade saw pictures of items belonging to her - also in a box delivered to Sebastian.

Bos Logistics did not reply to any of the emails sent to them asking for an explanation and to fix up their mess. They did not even get a response from either Shane nor Ciara. In a cell phone video taken by one of the disgruntled customers taken from the inside of a warehouse where Bos Logistics stores the content before being transported and shipped, one can clearly see there is no clear demarcation between the different client’s boxes and the shoddy wrapping of items. On the video a warehouse staff member can be heard to say “only Shane knows where everything is.” A clear indication of a logistical nightmare where the ground staff are not in control of the process.

Our story
With the evidence at hand we will now ask Shane O’Boyle to respond and request an interview. Should he be unwilling, we have three different addresses for the company and will be tracking him down at his warehouse, or office, or if that fails, we have a last option: His running route. He is a member of Strava fitness online App club posting his route and selfies.

Regarding the case studies: The first case study - Megan Ellis-Smith (who was interviewed already in March by Tim when Joy was planning to do the story) - was interviewed in person here in Muizenberg. The second case study, the Elson’s, will be interviewed via zoom and our third case study, two in Dubai and one in Canada, on a communal zoom interview in split screen.

Visuals of Bos Logistics warehouse in Cape Town were taken on a cellphone by one of the many complainants we have been in contact with on a communal WhatsApp group. It shows boxes being piled up haphazardly with no clear demarcation of goods between the different clients and destinations. We will also draw on the selection of images from our case studies who have provided us with the proof of their missing and mixed up items.

In only three years, Bos Logistics have taken many people for a ride and complaints on Hellopeter and Sireglo have increased giving the company a one star rating. We hope this story will make people aware of the pitfalls and to always select a company who has a solid track record and has been operating for a number of years.

We also found out that Bos Logistics lied about membership to two organisations: Seajet Logistics Network - an international platform in the freight forwarding industry and The International Association of Movers - the moving and forwarding industry’s largest global trade association. They are also not a member of the South African Association of Freight Forwarders who encourages integrity and professional conduct.

Script:


Script: Bos Logistics - international removers or scam artists
Duration: 10:25 minutes

V/O Moving house is considered one of the top 5 most stressful life events. And if that move is to another country, the last thing you want is to arrive without your most precious possessions, and the sentimental items that remind you of home and loved ones far away.

LINK: But then you happen upon a website that promises small enough to care, large enough to do it, let our family move yours and it seems like your moving challenges are being taken care of.

V/O But are they? We met several people who made the move abroad, whose challenges only got bigger:
Sebastian Dockter and Silvana Cretu emigrated to Canada.
Jade Rainbow, to Dubai.
Lilani and Jan van der Westhuizen, also to Dubai.

V/O All these people, excited at starting a new life, used a company called Bos Logistics to ship their possessions.

Jan van der Westhuizen: They were very fast to reply on emails initiality and give a quote initially basically after they packed our stuff they basically went off the radar.

Jade Rainbow: They came to the house, I was there, and they came with no pens, no markers to mark the boxes, they ran out of boxes. From that day I thought I knew it was just going to be a disaster.

Sebastian Dockter: Stuff was picked up. But then as everybody else experienced it is almost like they vanished. The communication collapsed.

V/O With so many complaints we wondered whether Bos Logistics’ director, Shane Bryan O’Boyle had an explanation. First though we tried to find out a little more about him.
V/O Shane is 26 years old.
He’s a keen runner
And clearly likes posting selfies…
Along with his sister, Ciara, he runs this 'family business' that promises to deliver for other South African families. During our investigation, even more people came forward to tell us their stories.

Up music

V/O Megan and Mike Ellis-Smith moved from Muizenberg to the UK.

Megan Ellis-Smith: So we sold our house and packed everything and included in that is our valuable furniture… It is not easy leaving your home, your country, your friends.

V/O They left in May 2021. Bos Logistics guaranteed they would be reunited with their possession by July… but it was not to be.

Megan Ellis-Smith: So we got hold of Ciara and I spoke to her on the phone, luckily I did get through to her, and she said it will be there by the end of October. So we waited some more! By this time Bos was starting to go underground and they wouldn’t answer emails.

V/O Until then the range of explanations, shipping delays, containers not offloaded, truck strikes, had been believable. Almost.

LINK: But after all the endless delays and excuses they discovered that their precious belongings had never left Cape town. They were still in the Bos Logistics warehouse.

V/O Megan and Mike were now on the warpath. They paid a visit to the warehouse to look for their belongings.

Megan: I was just gobsmacked. I haven’t seen anything like that. It was just filled to the ceiling with boxes and furniture and nothing was labeled

V/O The couple braved the mayhem. They eventually found most of their goods, which were then shipped quickly and efficiently by another removal company.

LINK: If you were to troll through the Bos Logistics website and letterheads you get the idea this is a thriving business with major offices in locations around the country and even overseas. Now this is the head office address that Shane gave us a few days ago. Let’s see what is happening.

Derek Watts: Good morning to you. We’ve come to see Shane.

Receptionist: He is on the line.

Derek Watts: He is on the line?

V/O After several minutes we were told that Shane was on a survey and not available to talk. Shane later said he was attending an emergency in port.

Derek: Where is everybody today? Why is there nobody here?

Receptionist: They are all out on jobs.

Derek Watts: Clients told us that the warehouse is a mess but this is just such a shock it is utter shambles. It is like a huge jumble sale gone wrong. Cartons spilling over, bits and pieces not marked. How anything can arrive in the right country at the right time is beyond me.

V/O No surprise, then, that the ‘logistics’ part of Bos Logistics failed dismally. Boxes destined for Canada ended up in Dubai and vice versa. Imagine opening your shipment and realising that not only isn’t it yours: it doesn’t even belong on your continent! This is exactly what happened to Sebastian who was sent some of Jan and Lilani's boxes.

Sebastian Dockter: So we put the stuff on facebook and sooner or later there was like other people. And then Jan and Lilani found their goods in our listing in things that did not belong to us.

Lilani van der Westhuizen: From the pictures it is clear that it is some very expensive kitchen equipment which we would really like to have and it is sitting in canada and it feels like we are never going to see it again.

Jade Rainbow: I went onto facebook and I went scrolling and I thought ‘o my gosh’ that’s my box. That’s my stuff sitting in Canada.

V/O Jade did eventually track down some of her belongings to a warehouse in Dubai.

Jade Rainbow: When I got there I knew some of my stuff was there because my daughter’s scooter was out, obviously the boxes that had my name on but you could see the other person’s name just in pen.

Derek: Jade it sounds like a disturbing game of pick a box!

Jade Rainbow: Yah basically yes. And I emailed Bos Logistics and I said: these are the pictures and the boxes in my name that don’t belong to me and they blamed it on looting.

Silvana Cretu: It is beyond stressful. Initially you open the boxes and it is just not your stuff.

Derek Watts: It’s other people’s stuff!

Silvana Cretu: You’re going through other people’s kitchen supplies and carpets then you realise they are feeling the same thing you are.

V/O As if complaints about delayed, nonexistent or wildly incorrect shipments weren’t enough, there was an allegation of fraud to be added. The Elsons moved from Table View to Dresden in Germany. It took nearly 12 months for their shipment to arrive. Many items were missing, and some were badly damaged. Luckily, they had insured their belongings. Or had they?

Wesley Elson: So we received a document indicating the amount we asked for with the OUTsurance logo on it, showing quite a bit of detail. My understanding was that this is the actual document from OUTsurance assuring us that our policy is in place.

Derek Watts: Quite a simple answer from OUTsurance “We do not offer marine insurance”. That is it.

Wesley Elson: That is my understanding. I also used the number that is on the document and OUTsurance told me there is no such policy with them at the time.

Derek: So did you take it up with Shane O’Boyle?

Wesley Elson: So we did not confront him directly. We had discussions with quite a few lawyers. The reason why we did not push ahead with it again, due to the cost.

Derek Watts: Did you ever get an explanation an apology?

Wesley Elson: No nothing.

V/O We were still trying to hunt Shane down. The office address in Claremont was next.

Derek: How are you doing?

Receptionist: Good and fine and you sir?

Derek Watts: We come to see Bos Logistics.

Receptionist: Not on our occupancy.

Derek Watts: So not listed on your tenant list?

Receptionist; No. They have a membership as we see on here. So membership means they can use the facility like there, sit in the co-working space.

Derek Watts: You don't get a permanent office space but you can bring clients here for a meeting and use the boardroom.

Receptionist; And you can use the address.

V/O Where to next? We tried Cape Town’s V&A Waterfront at the address on his email signature.

Derek Watts: So we are looking for Bos Logistics.

Receptionist: We actually don’t know where they are. There have been many people looking for them. We have emailed them, we tried WhatsApping them, no response.

V/O Another dead end! Where was Shane O’Boyle hiding?

Derek Watts: But we are not giving up in the search for Shane O’Boyle.
“This is the answering service for….”Please try again later”…. “The subscriber you have dialed is not available at present”
”All our assistants are unavailable at this time”
Derek Watts: So that was head office. We have run out of numbers. This is just pathetic.

V/O We emailed Shane a list of complaints. His response?
He said ‘Our team works around the clock’ to ensure loading integrity!
Shipping delays? He said they have experienced industry issues, volatility in demand changes, a shortage of containers, fewer vessels operating at slower speeds and struggling ports.
The careless approach to the job, ‘false’ says Shane who claims they take pride in caring for people’s belongings.
And what about the insurance? According to Shane, ‘they offer clients transit insurance, otherwise clients must self-insure or make alternative arrangements.’ Shane says they offer some payment for lost or damaged goods anyway’.
Regarding OUTsurance he said “I am aware that OUTsurance does not offer All Risk Marine Transit Insurance”. But he didn’t explain how a fake insurance policy was sent to Wesley Elson.

V/O Over and above the heartache and financial loss they’ve suffered these families have had to accept that some of their most sentimental possessions are gone forever.

Wesley Elson: I actually built a small table for my daughter when she was born. That is now missing.

Derek Watts: Do you think it is a scam or just incompetence?

Jade Rainbow: I feel that it is a bit of both, incompetence and scam. I feel I have been scammed.

Megan Ellis-Smith: I really feel very strongly that Bos has lied to us all the way, avoided us, and pretty much scammed us.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

PROMOS:
First promo: 22 Seconds
V/O Empty promises, outrageous delays, fake insurance and no one to answer for any of it. This is what dozens of Cape residents had to contend with after they hired a removal company to help them get settled in a new country.
Lilani van der Westhuizen: So this was really a very horrible experience. I think it is incompetence in the highest degree and they shouldn’t run a business.

Second promo: 22 Seconds
V/O Imagine opening your shipment and realising that not only isn’t it yours: it doesn’t even belong on your continent!
Jade Rainbow: And I went onto Facebook, and I went scrolling and I thought, Oh my gosh that’s my box. That’s my stuff sitting in Canada!
Derek Watts: Clients told us that the warehouse is a mess but this is just such a shock! It is utter shambles…

Third promo: 11 Seconds
V/O Moving abroad became a nightmare for dozens of people from the Cape who trusted their precious cargo with an international removal company and paid the price.

Our story With the evidence at hand we will now ask Shane O’Boyle to respond and request an interview. Should he be unwilling, we have three different addresses for the company and will be tracking him down at his warehouse, or office, or if that fails, we have a last option: His running route. And if that move is to another country, the last thing you want is to arrive without your most precious possessions, and the sentimental items that remind you of home and loved ones far away. LINK: But then you happen upon a website that promises small enough to care, large enough to do it, let our family move yours and it seems like your moving challenges are being taken care of. V/O But are they? We met several people who made the move abroad, whose challenges only got bigger: Sebastian Dockter and Silvana Cretu emigrated to Canada. Jade Rainbow, to Dubai. Lilani and Jan van der Westhuizen, also to Dubai. V/O All these people, excited at starting a new life, used a company called Bos Logistics to ship their possessions. Jan van der Westhuizen: They were very fast to reply on emails initiality and give a quote initially basically after they packed our stuff they basically went off the radar. Jade Rainbow: They came to the house, I was there, and they came with no pens, no markers to mark the boxes, they ran out of boxes. From that day I thought I knew it was just going to be a disaster. Sebastian Dockter: Stuff was picked up. But then as everybody else experienced it is almost like they vanished. The communication collapsed. V/O With so many complaints we wondered whether Bos Logistics’ director, Shane Bryan O’Boyle had an explanation. First though we tried to find out a little more about him. V/O Shane is 26 years old. He’s a keen runner And clearly likes posting selfies… Along with his sister, Ciara, he runs this 'family business' that promises to deliver for other South African families. During our investigation, even more people came forward to tell us their stories. Up music V/O Megan and Mike Ellis-Smith moved from Muizenberg to the UK. Megan Ellis-Smith: So we sold our house and packed everything and included in that is our valuable furniture… It is not easy leaving your home, your country, your friends. V/O They left in May 2021. Bos Logistics guaranteed they would be reunited with their possession by July… but it was not to be. Megan Ellis-Smith: So we got hold of Ciara and I spoke to her on the phone, luckily I did get through to her, and she said it will be there by the end of October. So we waited some more! By this time Bos was starting to go underground and they wouldn’t answer emails. V/O Until then the range of explanations, shipping delays, containers not offloaded, truck strikes, had been believable. Almost. LINK: But after all the endless delays and excuses they discovered that their precious belongings had never left Cape town. They were still in the Bos Logistics warehouse. V/O Megan and Mike were now on the warpath. They paid a visit to the warehouse to look for their belongings. Megan: I was just gobsmacked. I haven’t seen anything like that. It was just filled to the ceiling with boxes and furniture and nothing was labeled V/O The couple braved the mayhem. They eventually found most of their goods, which were then shipped quickly and efficiently by another removal company. LINK: If you were to troll through the Bos Logistics website and letterheads you get the idea this is a thriving business with major offices in locations around the country and even overseas. Now this is the head office address that Shane gave us a few days ago. Let’s see what is happening. Derek Watts: Good morning to you. We’ve come to see Shane. Receptionist: He is on the line. Derek Watts: He is on the line? V/O After several minutes we were told that Shane was on a survey and not available to talk. Shane later said he was attending an emergency in port. Derek: Where is everybody today? Why is there nobody here? Receptionist: They are all out on jobs. Derek Watts: Clients told us that the warehouse is a mess but this is just such a shock it is utter shambles. It is like a huge jumble sale gone wrong. Cartons spilling over, bits and pieces not marked. How anything can arrive in the right country at the right time is beyond me. V/O No surprise, then, that the ‘logistics’ part of Bos Logistics failed dismally. Boxes destined for Canada ended up in Dubai and vice versa. Imagine opening your shipment and realising that not only isn’t it yours: it doesn’t even belong on your continent! This is exactly what happened to Sebastian who was sent some of Jan and Lilani's boxes. Sebastian Dockter: So we put the stuff on facebook and sooner or later there was like other people. And then Jan and Lilani found their goods in our listing in things that did not belong to us. Lilani van der Westhuizen: From the pictures it is clear that it is some very expensive kitchen equipment which we would really like to have and it is sitting in canada and it feels like we are never going to see it again. Jade Rainbow: I went onto facebook and I went scrolling and I thought ‘o my gosh’ that’s my box. That’s my stuff sitting in Canada. V/O Jade did eventually track down some of her belongings to a warehouse in Dubai. Jade Rainbow: When I got there I knew some of my stuff was there because my daughter’s scooter was out, obviously the boxes that had my name on but you could see the other person’s name just in pen. Derek: Jade it sounds like a disturbing game of pick a box! Jade Rainbow: Yah basically yes. And I emailed Bos Logistics and I said: these are the pictures and the boxes in my name that don’t belong to me and they blamed it on looting. Silvana Cretu: It is beyond stressful. Initially you open the boxes and it is just not your stuff. Derek Watts: It’s other people’s stuff! Silvana Cretu: You’re going through other people’s kitchen supplies and carpets then you realise they are feeling the same thing you are. V/O As if complaints about delayed, nonexistent or wildly incorrect shipments weren’t enough, there was an allegation of fraud to be added. The Elsons moved from Table View to Dresden in Germany. It took nearly 12 months for their shipment to arrive. Many items were missing, and some were badly damaged. Luckily, they had insured their belongings. Or had they? Wesley Elson: So we received a document indicating the amount we asked for with the OUTsurance logo on it, showing quite a bit of detail. My understanding was that this is the actual document from OUTsurance assuring us that our policy is in place. Derek Watts: Quite a simple answer from OUTsurance “We do not offer marine insurance”. That is it. Wesley Elson: That is my understanding. I also used the number that is on the document and OUTsurance told me there is no such policy with them at the time. Derek: So did you take it up with Shane O’Boyle? Wesley Elson: So we did not confront him directly. We had discussions with quite a few lawyers. The reason why we did not push ahead with it again, due to the cost. Derek Watts: Did you ever get an explanation an apology? Wesley Elson: No nothing. V/O We were still trying to hunt Shane down. The office address in Claremont was next. Derek: How are you doing? Receptionist: Good and fine and you sir? Derek Watts: We come to see Bos Logistics. Receptionist: Not on our occupancy. Derek Watts: So not listed on your tenant list? Receptionist; No. They have a membership as we see on here. So membership means they can use the facility like there, sit in the co-working space. Derek Watts: You don't get a permanent office space but you can bring clients here for a meeting and use the boardroom. Receptionist; And you can use the address. V/O Where to next? We tried Cape Town’s V&A Waterfront at the address on his email signature. Derek Watts: So we are looking for Bos Logistics. Receptionist: We actually don’t know where they are. There have been many people looking for them. We have emailed them, we tried WhatsApping them, no response. V/O Another dead end! Where was Shane O’Boyle hiding? Derek Watts: But we are not giving up in the search for Shane O’Boyle. “This is the answering service for….”Please try again later”…. “The subscriber you have dialed is not available at present” ”All our assistants are unavailable at this time” Derek Watts: So that was head office. We have run out of numbers. This is just pathetic. V/O We emailed Shane a list of complaints. His response? He said ‘Our team works around the clock’ to ensure loading integrity! Shipping delays? He said they have experienced industry issues, volatility in demand changes, a shortage of containers, fewer vessels operating at slower speeds and struggling ports. The careless approach to the job, ‘false’ says Shane who claims they take pride in caring for people’s belongings. And what about the insurance? According to Shane, ‘they offer clients transit insurance, otherwise clients must self-insure or make alternative arrangements.’ Shane says they offer some payment for lost or damaged goods anyway’. Regarding OUTsurance he said “I am aware that OUTsurance does not offer All Risk Marine Transit Insurance”. But he didn’t explain how a fake insurance policy was sent to Wesley Elson. V/O Over and above the heartache and financial loss they’ve suffered these families have had to accept that some of their most sentimental possessions are gone forever. Wesley Elson: I actually built a small table for my daughter when she was born. That is now missing. Derek Watts: Do you think it is a scam or just incompetence? Jade Rainbow: I feel that it is a bit of both, incompetence and scam. I feel I have been scammed. Megan Ellis-Smith: I really feel very strongly that Bos has lied to us all the way, avoided us, and pretty much scammed us. _______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ PROMOS: First promo: 22 Seconds V/O Empty promises, outrageous delays, fake insurance and no one to answer for any of it. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Moving abroad became a nightmare for a number of people from the Cape who trusted their precious cargo with international removers Bos Logistics, and paid the price.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: How did one international removal company scam at least a dozen people we know of from Cape Town who planned to move abroad, into believing they are up to the job? Relocating to Canada, UAE, Germany, and England, the incompetence and skulduggery of Shane and Ciara O’Boyle left a trail of infuriated and disgruntled customers behind.
metadata.Summary: An international move can be stressful and leave many people anxious. Selecting a reliable mover, who has your best interest at heart, is therefore vital. Sadly, many people fall victim to attractive pay-off lines such as: “Small enough to care, large enough to do it”, and “let our family move yours” - comforting words from Bos Logistics to lure them in. Bos Logistics, an international relocation and freight forwarding Cape Town company was registered under the ownership of Shane Brown O’Boyle in February 2020. In 2019 26-year-old O’Boyle opened his doors for business together with his sister, Ciara. We track the stories of several Cape Tonian families who were charmed by the young and confident Shane. Soon after payment they came to realise it was all false promises of insurance cover and expected shipping and delivery dates. It was endless guessing of where exactly their furniture was at any given time: did it in fact leave Cape Town? At which port was it held? Why was it not released? And why did some of their consignments get mixed up and ended up on another continent at someone else’s address?
metadata.Further information: Case study one: Megan Ellis-Smith In 2020 Megan Ellis-Smith and her husband Mike decided to emigrate to the UK. The elderly couple were anxious about the move: “It is not easy leaving your home, your country, your friends. And going across to another country and starting again”, said Megan. Their son Paul, found Bos Logistics on the internet. “They sounded professional and friendly, so we were very happy.” The quote from Shane came to R137 000 for door to door service which Megan accepted. The couple left in May and were promised their furniture by July. In July a shortage of truck drivers in the Uk got the blame for non-delivery. In August they were told their furniture had arrived and were cleared by customs - no charge - which Megan thought suspicious as there is normally a fee involved. The next correspondence from Ciara was to inform them their goods were on a vessel but were not offloaded as it had skipped the port and there would be a six week delay. “So we waited some more. By this time Bos was starting to go underground and they wouldn’t answer emails, all their phone lines”, Megan said. With no communication Megan was at her wits end and asked a friend in Cape Town to visit their office in Claremont. All they found was an unmanned desk. Megan became very suspicious and found a contact in the shipping industry to enquire if there was in fact a vessel with their goods on board. She waited for feedback. By December Megan received a mail from Ciara to say the furniture was now on a ship called Santa Teresa, only to be told two days before the expected arrival date, that the booking was canceled. Megan and Mike then heard from their source that their goods never left Cape Town and were in fact still in fact sitting in Shane’s warehouse. “So then we sent an email to Shane to say will you release our things, otherwise we will expose you to the Cape Time, the Argus….Carte Blanche, Hellopeter, Wendy Knola, Cirello the whole tutie, and then they responded quickly. So they say we have a container going we can load your goods or we can release your goods so we say release!” said Megan. With the help of a new transport company from Cape Town the couple’s furniture were moved from Bos’s warehouse and shipped. It cost a mere R19 000 versus Bos’s R137 000 and it only took 5 weeks to arrive at their new home in the UK. “I feel very strongly that Bos has lied to us all the way, avoided us and pretty much scammed us.” Besides dealing with the traumatic experice of the removal company, they son Paul passed away the year they emigrated. Case study two: Christelle and Wesley Elson Christelle and Wesley Elson, a couple from Tableview in the Cape moved to Dresden Germany in September 2019. They contracted Bos Logistics to move their belongings - a company detail on Sierlo, an online platform providing online quotes and costs at the touch of a button. The site also provides reviews of companies but at the time there were hardly any as they were probably some of his earliest customers. (the company was only registered in 2020 but business started in 2019 as per the evidence of the Elson’s who contracted their services.) They were quoted R30 725 for a full door to door service. The quote came with Marine All Risk Cover from OUTsurance policy to the value of R150 000. This gave the couple piece of mind. In September Bos arrived at the Elson’s door to pack. Christelle remembered that first meetingg with Shane. “On the day they came to collect Shane was there to supervise and told us the packing list will be sent to us via email soon, that should have raised a red flag”. To this date they have not received the list. December, no delivery was made. January, a wage strike was blamed. In February an email from Shane made the Elson’s very nervous. “We were informed that our goods would not be released due to a financial hold placed on Bos Logistics account with FNB (reason for this was suspected fraud). As a result the MSC Pegasus sent our goods back to South Africa”, quoted from Shane’s email. Was this a delay tactic? Where were their goods now? Did it actually leave Cape Town? It took 9 months for their belongings to arrive. The couple were distressed. “Some items were missing which are totally irreplaceable”, said Christelle. Engagement and wedding photos; a nursery table handcrafted by a devoted father for his daughter made from American Ash were amongst the missing items. “We immediately informed Shane that we would like to proceed with a claim to the insurance” said Wesley. To their shock, OUTsurance had no such policy on record. In an email OUTsurance confirmed “the document is not authentic” and “we do not have marine insurance”. They will be reporting Bos Logistics to the Crime Insurance Bureau for producing a fraudulent document under their name. Case study three: Split frame: Jan van der Westhuizen and Jade Rainbow from Dubai, and Sebastian Dockter from Canada Sharing a container saves cost, which is why Jan van der Westhuizen, Jade Rainbow, and a third person from the Cape emigrating, shared a container. Destination? United Arab Emirates. In October the container were offloaded at the Jebel Ali Port in Dubai and their goods were stored in a warehouse nearby. In the warehouse Jade was shocked at the condition in which she found her boxes. Items were peeling out and badly damaged. On closer inspection she even found a stranger’s goods inside. Toys belonging to her daughter were lying loose and some boxes were missing. Jan found many of his boxes missing! It took much searching and eventually he used the internet as a tool. He found a Facebook page “Lost and found, Bos Logistics South Africa” started by Sebastian Dockter, another South African who relocated to Canada. He identified several of his items on the site and contacted Sebatian who told him ten of Jan’s boxes were delivered to his house marked Sebastian! Fortunately for Sebastian, one of his boxes was amongst Jan’s goods. At the same time Jade saw pictures of items belonging to her - also in a box delivered to Sebastian. Bos Logistics did not reply to any of the emails sent to them asking for an explanation and to fix up their mess. They did not even get a response from either Shane nor Ciara. In a cell phone video taken by one of the disgruntled customers taken from the inside of a warehouse where Bos Logistics stores the content before being transported and shipped, one can clearly see there is no clear demarcation between the different client’s boxes and the shoddy wrapping of items. On the video a warehouse staff member can be heard to say “only Shane knows where everything is.” A clear indication of a logistical nightmare where the ground staff are not in control of the process. Our story With the evidence at hand we will now ask Shane O’Boyle to respond and request an interview. Should he be unwilling, we have three different addresses for the company and will be tracking him down at his warehouse, or office, or if that fails, we have a last option: His running route. He is a member of Strava fitness online App club posting his route and selfies. It shows boxes being piled up haphazardly with no clear demarcation of goods between the different clients and destinations. We will also draw on the selection of images from our case studies who have provided us with the proof of their missing and mixed up items. In only three years, Bos Logistics have taken many people for a ride and complaints on Hellopeter and Sireglo have increased giving the company a one star rating. We hope this story will make people aware of the pitfalls and to always select a company who has a solid track record and has been operating for a number of years.
